summary: Henry George Keene worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at Fort William College and Sidney Sussex College, Cambridge, later serving with the East India Company and as Professor at East India Company College (1824–1834).

Henry Hamilton Hadley specialized in religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Yale, Andover Theological Seminary, and Union Theological Seminary, and held posts as instructor and professor of Hebrew at Union Theological Seminary and Yale Divinity School (1858–1864).

Henry Herbert Dodwell was an Indologist and historian who studied at Lord Williams's School and St John's College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Education Service (1908–1922) and as professor at SOAS University of London (1922–1946).
Henry M. Hoenigswald was a linguist who studied at the universities of Munich, Zurich, Padua, and Florence. He held a long-term academic post at the University of Pennsylvania (~1948–1985).
Henry Martyn worked in linguistics and religious studies. He was educated at Truro Cathedral School and St John's College, and studied under John Borthwick Gilchrist around 1804–1805.
Henry Miers Elliot, a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology, was educated at Winchester College. He served as a civil servant for the East India Company from circa 1826 to 1853.
Henry Pitts Forster worked in Indology and linguistics. He served in the East India Company's Bengal Civil Service (~1783–1815) and was appointed Master of the Calcutta Mint in 1803.

Henry Rawlinson specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, archaeology, and linguistics. Educated at Great Ealing School and Middlesex University, he served in the East India Company, the Foreign Office, and led the Royal Asiatic and Royal Geographical Societies.
Henry Steel Olcott was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who attended Columbia University (~1847–1849). He co-founded the Theosophical Society in 1875.
Henry Sullivan Jarrett was an Indologist and historian. He served as Secretary and Member of the Board of Examiners at Fort William from circa 1870 to 1892, succeeding Heinrich Blochmann.

Henry Thomas Colebrooke was an Indologist who studied under Citrapati. He served with the East India Company, taught at Fort William College (1782–1814), and held leadership posts at the Royal Asiatic Society and Royal Astronomical Society.
Heramba Chandra Chackravarty was an Indology scholar who studied under Manindra Mohan Bose and served as a Lecturer at City College, Kolkata (attested 1977).

Herbert Cushing Tolman specialized in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Yale and held academic posts at Yale, Wisconsin-Madison, North Carolina at Chapel Hill, and Vanderbilt University (1894–1923).

Herbert Franke studied Sinology and history at Bonn, Berlin, and Cologne under Erich Haenisch and Erich Hauer. He served as professor at the University of Munich (1952–1979) and president of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1980–1985).
Herbert Hope Risley was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his education at Winchester College (~1863–1869) and New College (~1869–1873).

Herbert Härtel worked in Indology and archaeology. He studied at Halle and Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt, later serving as Director of the Museum of Asian Art (1963–1986) and professor at the Free University of Berlin (1965–1986).

Herbert Niel Randle was an Indologist and philosopher. He served as professor of philosophy at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1910–1927) and later as Librarian of the India Office Library (1927–1949).

Herbert V. Günther studied Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy at Munich and Vienna under Wilhelm Geiger and Wilhelm Havers. He held posts at Lucknow, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and headed Far Eastern Studies at the University of Saskatchewan (1964–1984).

Herbert Weir Smyth was a linguist and historian educated at Swarthmore, Harvard, Leipzig, and Göttingen under Hermann Sauppe. He held academic posts at Williams, Bryn Mawr, and Harvard University (from 1901).
Herman Kellgren was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus, Eugène Burnouf, and Philippe Édouard Foucaux. He held a post at the University of Helsinki (~1849–1856).
